correctness.rationale: Norm dissipation gives \(Q_m=2\eta\int_0^\infty|A_m(t)|^2dt\). The scalar rank-one free resolvent gives a Laplace transform with a square-root spectral band. Plancherel splits it into a source-independent band integral and a strictly positive exponential exterior integral. Its endpoint expansion yields explicit \(m^{-2}\) and \(m^{-4}\) coefficients, with an \(O(m^{-6})\) remainder. The band integral has an elementary exact evaluation. Its derivative is negative for normalized rate at least 1; below 1, the derivative sign is a series with a single negative constant followed by positive coefficients, giving exactly one global optimum. Independent spectral quadratures and direct finite-time tight-binding propagations in verify.py pass; finite computations are not treated as the proof.

value.rationale: The proportion of remote quantum walkers captured by a local optical loss site is a natural transport-efficiency quantity and loss strength is directly controllable. The theorem finds a unique dimensionless optimizer at an unexpected non-unit value, separating interior-trap geometry from the unit matching of a boundary sink, and quantifies how finite launch distance approaches the limiting efficiency with a universal inverse-square law. This is a complete natural design-parameter classification, rather than a trivial sign or normalization check.
